lessons.title: Create your first agent
lessons.summary: Paste your website address and your agent reads your pages. No code is needed.

steps.title: Open Agents
steps.body: From the sidebar, open Agents and create a new agent.

steps.title: Name your agent
steps.body: Choose the name carefully. It cannot be changed after the agent is created.

steps.title: Add your website
steps.body: Paste your website address. Steps AI reads your pages, documents and FAQs.

steps.title: Test it
steps.body: Open the preview chat and ask the questions your customers ask most.

callouts.text: The agent name is the one setting you cannot change later.

lessons.title: Add your business information
lessons.summary: Websites, files and FAQs live in Resources and can be shared by every agent.

steps.title: Open Resources
steps.body: Everything your agents know lives here.

steps.title: Add sources
steps.body: Add website pages, upload files or write FAQs.

steps.title: Choose the agents
steps.body: Pick which agents use each resource.

steps.title: Keep it current
steps.body: Update a resource once and every agent that uses it answers with the new information.

table.caption: Storage and crawls grow with your plan

callouts.text: Keep prices, dates and policies current in your documents so answers stay accurate.

lessons.title: Set your agent's tone and guardrails
lessons.summary: Personas set your agent's role, tone and the things it must never do.

steps.title: Open Personas
steps.body: Choose a predefined persona or create your own.

steps.title: Pick a tone
steps.body: Friendly, professional, direct or neutral. Professional is the default.

steps.title: Add guardrails
steps.body: For example: never quote prices, never give medical, legal or financial advice, never discuss politics.

steps.title: Or generate it
steps.body: Generate a persona with AI from your homepage, the agent's role, your audience and your guardrails.

callouts.text: Healthcare and finance businesses should always add the matching "never give advice" guardrail.

lessons.title: Add the chat widget to your website
lessons.summary: Copy one script, use a framework snippet, or install the WordPress plugin.

steps.title: Open Website
steps.body: Find the install options for your agent.

steps.title: Copy the script
steps.body: Use the universal script, or the snippet for HTML, React, Next.js, Vue or Angular.

steps.title: Paste it into your site
steps.body: Guides cover Wix, Webflow, Framer, Bubble and WordPress.

steps.title: Limit where it runs
steps.body: Add allowed domains so the widget only works on your own sites.

table.caption: Where to paste the script
rows: Custom code, end of body, then save and publish
Project settings, custom code, then publish
Use the Steps AI plugin instead of a script

callouts.text: If you leave allowed domains empty, the widget can be embedded on any website.

lessons.title: Install the WordPress plugin
lessons.summary: WordPress can remove script tags from pages. The plugin avoids that.

steps.title: Download the plugin
steps.body: It comes pre-loaded with your agent.

steps.title: Upload it
steps.body: In WordPress, add a new plugin and upload the file.

steps.title: Activate it
steps.body: The widget appears on your site. You never touch code.

lessons.title: Customise the widget
lessons.summary: Match your brand and keep the widget out of the way on mobile.

steps.title: Brand it
steps.body: Set your logo, colours, light or dark theme, title and greeting.

steps.title: Add quick questions
steps.body: Up to five, so visitors know what to ask.

steps.title: Choose the display
steps.body: Floating widget or inline search bar, set separately for desktop and mobile.

steps.title: Place it
steps.body: Pick one of nine positions and when it appears.

table.caption: Display options
rows: Floating widget or inline search bar
Straight away, 5 seconds, 10 seconds, 30 seconds or 1 minute

callouts.text: Quick questions are the most useful field on this screen and the most often skipped.
On mobile, keep the bubble clear of your add-to-cart button.

lessons.title: Connect your WhatsApp Business number
lessons.summary: Connect through Meta's official API. The same connection covers Instagram and Messenger.
before: Access to your Meta business account

steps.title: Open WhatsApp
steps.body: Start the Meta connection.

steps.title: Sign in with Meta
steps.body: Allow access to your WhatsApp Business account.

steps.title: Choose the agent
steps.body: Pick which agent answers on this number.

steps.title: Send a test
steps.body: Message the number from your own phone before customers do.

callouts.text: How many conversations you can start each day follows WhatsApp's messaging tiers for your number.

lessons.title: Use approved message templates
lessons.summary: Messages that start a conversation use templates that Meta approves first.

steps.title: Write the template
steps.body: Keep it short and add personalised fields such as the first name.

steps.title: Submit for approval
steps.body: Meta reviews each template before you can use it.

steps.title: Use it
steps.body: Approved templates appear in campaigns and workflows.

callouts.text: Replies inside an open conversation do not need a template.

lessons.title: Reply to missed WhatsApp calls
lessons.summary: When you miss a call, send a WhatsApp message so the conversation can continue in chat.

steps.title: Switch it on
steps.body: Turn on the missed-call reply for your number.

steps.title: Write the message
steps.body: For example: Sorry we missed your call. How can we help?

steps.title: Let the agent continue
steps.body: When the customer replies, your agent takes it from there.

lessons.title: Connect Instagram and Messenger
lessons.summary: One Meta sign-in covers your Instagram professional account and your Facebook page.
before: Admin access to your Facebook page

steps.title: Open Instagram or Messenger
steps.body: Start the Meta connection.

steps.title: Sign in with Meta
steps.body: Allow access to your Instagram account and Facebook page.

steps.title: Choose the agent
steps.body: Pick which agent answers your DMs and page messages.

callouts.text: Instagram broadcast campaigns are not available. Campaigns run on WhatsApp.

lessons.title: Turn Instagram comments into DMs
lessons.summary: When someone comments a keyword, reply in their direct messages straight away.

steps.title: Add a keyword
steps.body: For example, PRICE or LINK.

steps.title: Write the reply
steps.body: This is the first DM the person receives.

steps.title: Choose the posts
steps.body: Run it on all posts, or one post or Reel, including live comments.

steps.title: Add quick replies
steps.body: Buttons wait for the customer's choice and branch on it.

callouts.text: On Instagram, replying from the Instagram app pauses the AI so it does not talk over you.

lessons.title: Publish a chat page
lessons.summary: No website? Share a branded page with your agent on it.

steps.title: Create the page
steps.body: Open your agent's site settings.

steps.title: Brand it
steps.body: Logo, colours for light and dark, welcome message, up to five suggested questions.

steps.title: Add link cards
steps.body: Link your catalogue, booking page or socials.

steps.title: Publish and share
steps.body: Preview on desktop and mobile, then share the link in your bio or status.

callouts.text: The page uses a public link on the Steps AI domain. Custom domains are not set up from this screen today.

lessons.title: Connect an app
lessons.summary: Connecting is one step. Switching it on for an agent is the second.

steps.title: Open Apps
steps.body: Every integration starts here.

steps.title: Choose the app
steps.body: Search the library and select it.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Sign in, or enter your account details, to connect it to your workspace.

steps.title: Switch it on
steps.body: Turn it on for each agent that should use it.

steps.title: Test it
steps.body: Ask a real question in the preview chat.

table.caption: The 21 apps you can connect
rows: Shiprocket, Delhivery, DTDC, iThink Logistics, WareIQ
Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar, Calendly, Cal.com, Square Appointments
Google Drive, Google Sheets, Notion, Airtable

callouts.text: An app that is connected but not switched on for an agent does nothing. This is the most common setup question.
Need an app that is not listed? Ask for a custom integration from the Channels area.

lessons.title: Share order status from your store and courier
lessons.summary: Your agent reads the order from your store and the status from your delivery tool.

steps.title: Connect your store
steps.body: Shopify or WooCommerce.

steps.title: Connect your courier
steps.body: Shiprocket, Delhivery, DTDC, iThink Logistics or WareIQ.

steps.title: Switch both on
steps.body: Turn them on for your support agent.

steps.title: Test with a real order
steps.body: Ask "Where is my order" with an order number.

callouts.text: The agent shares the status your store and courier report. It cannot change a delivery.

lessons.title: Save leads to HubSpot
lessons.summary: Already use HubSpot? Your agent can save leads there instead of the built-in CRM.

steps.title: Connect HubSpot
steps.body: Sign in and allow access.

steps.title: Switch it on
steps.body: Turn it on for the agents that collect leads.

steps.title: Check a test lead
steps.body: Share your details in the preview chat and find the record in HubSpot.

lessons.title: Book appointments into your calendar
lessons.summary: The booking skill works with Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar, Calendly, Cal.com and Square Appointments.

steps.title: Connect your calendar
steps.body: Do this once for the workspace.

steps.title: Switch on the skill
steps.body: Turn on Book appointment for your agent.

steps.title: Choose the calendar
steps.body: Each booking skill uses one calendar provider.

steps.title: Choose the details
steps.body: Name, email, company or job title. Switch each one on or off.

callouts.text: You can connect several calendars and choose one per booking skill.

lessons.title: Create tickets from conversations
lessons.summary: Collect the details your team needs, then notify the right people.

steps.title: Switch on Create ticket
steps.body: Find it with the other skills.

steps.title: Choose the fields
steps.body: Text, long text, number, email, phone, dropdown or media, such as a photo.

steps.title: Mark required fields
steps.body: The agent asks until required fields are filled.

steps.title: Add recipients
steps.body: Everyone listed gets an email for each new ticket.

lessons.title: Write rules for when a skill is used
lessons.summary: Plain-English rules and examples stop a skill firing at the wrong moment.

steps.title: Say when to use it
steps.body: Describe the situation in one or two sentences.

steps.title: Add “should trigger” examples
steps.body: Messages that should trigger the skill.

steps.title: Add should-not examples
steps.body: Messages that look similar but should not, with a reason.

callouts.text: Clear should-not examples are the fastest way to stop a skill being used by mistake.

lessons.title: Build a custom skill
lessons.summary: An AI skill follows your instructions. A flow skill collects details and calls an app or webhook.

steps.title: Name it and pick a kind
steps.body: AI skill or flow skill.

steps.title: Write the trigger examples
steps.body: When should the agent use it?

steps.title: Add instructions or a flow
steps.body: AI instructions, or the fields to collect and the HTTP request or app action to run.

lessons.title: Set up human handoff
lessons.summary: Decide how long customers wait, what they see and who gets told.

steps.title: Switch on handoff
steps.body: Turn on Hand over to a person.

steps.title: Set the wait time
steps.body: How long the customer waits for a person before the fallback message.

steps.title: Write the fallback
steps.body: What customers see if nobody joins in time.

steps.title: Choose who is told
steps.body: Add the people who get an email when someone needs your team.

table.caption: Handoff settings
rows: Any recipients. Leave it empty to turn alerts off.

callouts.text: Human handoff starts from the Starter plan.

lessons.title: Pick up a live request
lessons.summary: When a customer asks for a person, the request appears in your CRM with the full chat.

steps.title: Open Live requests
steps.body: Every request for a person, with its reason and priority.

steps.title: Claim it
steps.body: A team member claims the conversation so customers are not answered twice.

steps.title: Reply with context
steps.body: The full conversation is already there.

lessons.title: Send a WhatsApp campaign
lessons.summary: Send an approved template to a chosen audience. Replies go to your agent.

steps.title: Pick the agent
steps.body: Choose the agent that handles replies.

steps.title: Choose the template
steps.body: Only approved templates appear.

steps.title: Choose the audience
steps.body: A saved list, a CSV, Shopify customers or a single tag.

steps.title: Review and send
steps.body: Check the estimated cost, then send now or schedule it.

callouts.text: A single campaign can currently go to up to 1,000 people.

lessons.title: Start with a workflow template
lessons.summary: Cart recovery, order updates and team alerts, from menus, not code.

steps.title: Browse templates
steps.body: Pick the job you want to automate.

steps.title: Rename it
steps.body: Give it a name before you create it.

steps.title: Review each step
steps.body: Waits, conditions and messages are all editable.

steps.title: Switch it on
steps.body: Workflows stay as drafts until you activate them.

table.caption: Popular templates
rows: Reminds shoppers who left items in their cart
Shares shipping updates, then asks for a review
Tells your team about large orders

callouts.text: Most templates today are built for Shopify stores.
WhatsApp Cart Recovery does not yet remove duplicates, so several add-to-cart events can send several messages.

lessons.title: Triggers and steps in the builder
lessons.summary: Every workflow starts with a trigger and runs steps you choose from menus.

steps.title: Choose a trigger
steps.body: What starts the workflow.

steps.title: Add steps
steps.body: Wait, check a condition, send a message, call another tool or end.

steps.title: Set error handling
steps.body: Each step can fail, skip or retry.

table.caption: Builder building blocks
rows: Message received, manual, schedule, webhook, app event, form submission

lessons.title: Find the conversations that need you
lessons.summary: Filter the inbox by channel, agent, tag, unread or starred.

steps.title: Open Inbox
steps.body: Every agent and channel together.

steps.title: Filter
steps.body: By channel, agent or tag, such as refund request or new lead.

steps.title: Star what matters
steps.body: Come back to it later from the starred filter.

callouts.text: Each agent also has its own conversation view.

lessons.title: Use conversation tags
lessons.summary: Every conversation is tagged automatically, so you can count, filter and target it.

steps.title: Review the tags
steps.body: Each has a category, description and a plain-English rule.

steps.title: Edit or add tags
steps.body: Write the rule for when a conversation gets the tag.

steps.title: Use them
steps.body: Filter the inbox, read analytics or send a campaign to one tag.

table.caption: Tag categories
rows: Paid social, Google ads, organic website
Billing question, refund request, technical issue

lessons.title: Use the built-in CRM
lessons.summary: Customers, tickets and live requests, each in its own table.

steps.title: Open CRM
steps.body: Start from the overview.

steps.title: Switch tables
steps.body: Customers, Tickets or Live requests.

steps.title: Pick your columns
steps.body: Show what your team needs.

steps.title: Add custom fields
steps.body: Label, type, placeholder and required setting.

callouts.text: There is no limit on the number of contacts.

lessons.title: Read your analytics
lessons.summary: See volume, response time, channels and the hours customers message.

steps.title: Pick a date range
steps.body: Today, 7 or 30 days, a month or custom.

steps.title: Choose the agent
steps.body: All agents or one.

steps.title: Read the headline numbers
steps.body: Chats, messages and average AI response time.

steps.title: Find busy hours
steps.body: The activity heat map shows days and hours.

callouts.text: Average response time measures the AI agent, not your team.
State-level location is available for website chats only.

lessons.title: How credits work
lessons.summary: A credit is not a reply. The model your agent uses sets the cost of each reply.

steps.title: Credits come with your plan
steps.body: Each plan includes a monthly number of credits.

steps.title: Each reply uses credits
steps.body: Lighter models use fewer credits per reply than larger ones.

steps.title: You choose the model
steps.body: Set it per agent.

steps.title: Watch usage live
steps.body: Credits, storage and crawls are tracked.

callouts.text: Extra credit packs expire at the end of your billing cycle.

lessons.title: What each plan includes
lessons.summary: Free is for trying the agent. Order tracking, handoff and channels start on Starter.

steps.title: Compare plans
steps.body: See current prices on the pricing page.

lessons.title: Cancel or change your plan
lessons.summary: Cancel at any time. Your plan stays active until the end of the period.

steps.title: Open Billing

steps.title: Change or cancel
steps.body: Your plan stays active until the end of the billing period.

steps.title: Export your data

callouts.text: Payments are not refunded, and unused credits do not carry over.
